text: Futures: ratings now move with who has actually been playing (each team's last five lineups, valued player by player), so trades, call-ups and returning players count straight away; better in 7 of 10 replayed seasons. The in-season rating now weights goals 80% and expected goals 20% (was 60/40 by judgement; fitted on ten seasons).

Futures now account for injuries: each player on the injury list lowers his team's rating for the games he is expected to miss, priced by how much missing players changed results in 12,572 games (2015-2025). A new section on the futures page shows each team's absences next to its chances without them.

Futures: playoff series now use shot differential instead of goal differential, and favourites count for more in the playoffs early in the season. Cup and conference chances were more accurate in 8 of 10 replayed seasons; regular-season chances are unchanged.

Futures page: a candidate model that gives favourites more weight in the playoffs early in the season is shown next to the live Final and Cup chances (replays found early Cup chances too flat; the live model is unchanged).

Awards page: chances of leading the league in passing yards, passing TDs, rushing yards, receiving yards, receptions and sacks, tested on 2012–2025. Rookie awards and Offensive Player chances sharpen from week 8 after a weekly replay showed late favourites were too cautious.

Futures page: a candidate model with a bigger playoff home edge is shown next to the live model for conference and Super Bowl chances (it was more accurate in 10 of 13 replayed seasons; the live model is unchanged).
Award chances now simulate each candidate's season to the end and apply the 65-game rule; MVP and Defensive Player chances are shown before the season. Tested on 2010–2026.

Award chances replayed on 2011–2026 from dated season-to-date numbers: Art Ross and Rocket Richard races tightened, Vezina sharper late, and an early-season caution added (early favourites won much less often than shown).
Brownlow chances widened after a round-by-round replay showed favourites were far too short; the Coleman table now gives each player's chance of kicking the most goals.

History pages now include a Live check: this season's published forecasts are scored as results come in (NFL games already; futures once a season is half played), including the archived challenger models.

NFL now has a week-by-week History page: the model replayed for every week of 2022 to 2025, with a note on how much to trust each market. Only four seasons, so treat it as a rough guide. The live season will be added as it is played.
History pages now keep the live season: each refresh with new numbers is archived, so you can look back at what the site showed for any week of this season (NBA, NHL, AFL, NBL).
Week-by-week history page: championship, Grand Final, top 2, minor premier and finals chances for each week of 13 past seasons, with movement and a reliability note.
Round-by-round history page: every team's premiership, Grand Final, top 4, top 8 and finals chances after each round of 14 past seasons, with movement and a reliability note.

Week-by-week history page: every team's title, conference, division, top-seed and playoff chance for each week of 14 past seasons, with 1- and 4-week movement and a reliability note (also NHL, 10 seasons).
Back-test now uses one league-wide checkpoint date (the old split gave wrong game counts for many teams); 20-game playoff score is 0.428 over 2021-25, not the 0.415 shown before.
Winner trends page: what national champions, finalists and playoff teams had in common (2014 onward).
Havoc rate (sacks, tackles for loss, pass breakups, turnovers) on team pages, plus havoc plays per defender on the players page.
Hustle stats (deflections, loose balls, box-outs) and Synergy play-type stats for teams and players, from 2015-16.
Preseason playoff and conference probabilities are less overconfident (tested over 14 seasons); fades out by game 16.
Fixed extra games showing in 2025-26 regular-season game logs (finals and play-in games now kept separate).
College football (FBS) advanced team and player stats and 12 seasons of history.
Assist-to-turnover ratio and assists as a share of made field goals for teams, players and game logs (also NBL).
Game logs now use official full-game team totals, backfilled for all 15 seasons.
Availability page: injured players' points value and games affected, now feeding the season simulation.
